chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Upon the first-timer (Al-Saroura) is that he shaves his head completely and does not merely shorten (the hair), and indeed, shortening is for the one who has performed Hajj (before).

key_terms.التَّقْصِير: Shortening (cutting hair to a specific length, not shaving)
key_terms.الصَّرُورَة: The first-timer (one performing Hajj for the first time)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between shaving and shortening hair for first-time Hajj pilgrims?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that pilgrims performing Hajj al-Tamattu' or Qiran must shave their heads completely (Qaza') rather than merely shortening the hair (Taqseer), a distinction rooted in the specific obligations of these Hajj types. This ruling highlights the scholarly consensus that the full shaving is a unique requirement for first-time pilgrims of these forms, whereas those who have performed Hajj previously are permitted to shorten their hair, reflecting the graduated ease in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Upon ‘Al-Saroura’ (the first-timer) is that he shaves off his head and must not do Taqseer (cutting some hair or finger nails). But rather, the Taqseer the is for the one who had (already) performed Hajj, the Hajj of Al-Islam’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Al-Sarura (one who performs al-Hajj for the first time) must shave his head and must not do Taqsir (cutting some hair or finger nails and so on); it is for those who have already performed Hajjahta al-Islam.’”
